title: Enterprise MCP tool hub
tagline: Company tools for Claude and every other agent, behind one door with scopes and a log.
summary: Domain teams publish typed MCP servers for their systems. Agent clients reach them only through an authorization server and a policy gateway that binds tokens to an audience, enforces per-tool scopes and rate limits, brokers backend credentials and records every call.
customer_job: Let employees use Claude, coding agents and internal agents against company systems without handing out API keys.
baseline: Teams paste API tokens into local configs; nobody can say which agent called which system with whose authority.
accepted_result: An agent action that the security team can attribute to a person, a client and a scope, and that the tool owner approved.

primary_metric.name: Governed tool calls
primary_metric.definition: Share of agent-to-system calls that pass through the hub with a bound token, scope check and audit record.

economics.basis: Illustrative assumption; value counted per agent task that completes using a governed tool instead of manual lookup.

components.label: Agent clients
components.detail: Claude, coding agents, internal agents acting for a person.

components.label: Tool catalog and consent

components.label: Content guardrail

components.label: Domain MCP servers
components.detail: CRM, tickets, docs, HR read-only; owned by domain teams.

components.label: Credential broker

components.label: Systems of record
components.detail: Unchanged backends with their own permissions.

components.label: Tool registry
components.detail: Tool versions, owners, scopes, approval state.

components.label: Audit ledger
components.detail: Who, which client, which tool, which scope, result.

components.label: Tool owners
components.detail: Approve new tools and scope changes.

components.label: Tool contract tests
components.detail: Schema, permission and denial tests per tool version.

journey.title: Discover and consent
journey.narration: A client lists tools, then the person grants specific scopes. The token names the hub as its only audience.

journey.title: Admit the call
journey.narration: Edge rate limits apply first. The gateway checks scope, tool version and input schema against the registry.

journey.title: Scan what goes in and out
journey.narration: Inputs and outputs are scanned for secrets and instruction-shaped text before they reach a system or a model.

journey.title: Act as the person, not as a robot
journey.narration: The server exchanges the token for a short-lived backend credential, so the system of record applies its own permissions.

journey.title: Record and govern
journey.narration: Every call is attributable. Tool owners approve new tools and scope changes in the registry.

journey.title: Test every tool version
journey.narration: Contract tests prove schemas, denials and scopes before a version is published.

team.step: Employee grants scopes to a client and uses tools through it
Agent calls tools; never sees backend credentials
Gateway enforces scopes, quotas and the kill switch
Tool owners approve tools and scope changes
Security reviews anomalies and revokes tokens

items: Read CRM accounts you can see

evals.name: Unauthorized calls
evals.threshold: 0 calls succeed without the required scope
evals.method: Scope-matrix tests per tool and client.

evals.name: Token audience binding
evals.method: Replay tokens minted for other servers.

evals.name: Schema conformance
evals.threshold: 100 percent of published tools pass contract tests
evals.method: Generated cases from each tool's input schema.

risks.risk: A server acts with its own broad credentials instead of the user's.
risks.control: Token exchange per call; no static backend keys in servers.

risks.risk: Tool output carries instructions into the agent.
risks.control: Output scanning and labelling of tool results as data.
Network policy allows backend access only from registered servers.

gcp.headline: Apigee in front of Cloud Run MCP servers
gcp.notes: Apigee enforces OAuth, quotas and policies; servers run on Cloud Run with workload identity; BigQuery holds the audit trail.
gcp.rationale: Enterprise API governance already in place for many estates; MCP-specific policy is configuration work.

vercel.headline: MCP routes on Vercel Functions with an external authorization server
vercel.notes: MCP servers deploy as functions; Edge Config holds the tool allowlist and kill switch so policy changes apply without a redeploy.
vercel.rationale: Fast for product teams; enterprise authorization and credential brokering come from partners.

cloudflare.headline: MCP servers on Workers with OAuth and Access
cloudflare.notes: Workers host remote MCP servers with an OAuth provider library; Access applies workforce identity; AI Gateway guardrails can scan model-bound content.
cloudflare.rationale: Strong edge controls and low cost per call; credential brokering to legacy systems is custom.

aws.headline: AgentCore Gateway and Identity with Lambda targets
aws.notes: AgentCore Gateway turns Lambda functions and APIs into MCP tools with identity propagation.

azure.headline: API Management exposing MCP with Entra ID
azure.notes: API Management can front MCP servers and existing APIs with Entra-issued tokens and per-product quotas.
azure.rationale: Natural for Entra estates; confirm MCP feature support for the API Management tier.

railway.headline: MCP server services behind a self-run gateway
railway.notes: Each domain server is a service; the gateway and authorization server are open-source components you operate.
